scope: All explicit setting bindings in the six process-page builders without mode or feature-condition filtering; includes disabled and conditional fields. Not a live inspection of user preset values.

settings.label: Layer height
settings.tooltip: L("This is the height for each layer. Smaller layer heights give greater accuracy but longer printing time.")
settings.handling: Resolve first-printing height including adaptive/sublayer changes; later-layer height is not a substitute. Block mixed-color sublayers from ordinary knee learning.

settings.label: First layer height
settings.tooltip: L("Height of the first layer. Making the first layer height thicker can improve build plate adhesion.")
settings.handling: Resolve first-printing height including adaptive/sublayer changes; later-layer height is not a substitute. Block mixed-color sublayers from ordinary knee learning.

settings.label: Mixed color sublayer
settings.tooltip: L("Enable mixed color sublayer splitting. When enabled, layers containing mixed color " "filaments will be split into sub-layers to achieve color mixing effects.")
settings.handling: Resolve first-printing height including adaptive/sublayer changes; later-layer height is not a substitute. Block mixed-color sublayers from ordinary knee learning.

settings.label: Default
settings.tooltip: L("Default line width if other line widths are set to 0. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Resolve default/percentage/auto widths and each extrusion role; measure emitted segment width rather than use one global width.

settings.label: First layer
settings.tooltip: L("Line width of the first layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Resolve default/percentage/auto widths and each extrusion role; measure emitted segment width rather than use one global width.

settings.label: Outer wall
settings.tooltip: L("Line width of outer wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Resolve default/percentage/auto widths and each extrusion role; measure emitted segment width rather than use one global width.

settings.label: Inner wall
settings.tooltip: L("Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Resolve default/percentage/auto widths and each extrusion role; measure emitted segment width rather than use one global width.

settings.label: Top surface
settings.tooltip: L("Line width for top surfaces. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Resolve default/percentage/auto widths and each extrusion role; measure emitted segment width rather than use one global width.

settings.label: Sparse infill
settings.tooltip: L("Line width of internal sparse infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Resolve default/percentage/auto widths and each extrusion role; measure emitted segment width rather than use one global width.

settings.label: Internal solid infill
settings.tooltip: L("Line width of internal solid infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Resolve default/percentage/auto widths and each extrusion role; measure emitted segment width rather than use one global width.

settings.label: Support
settings.tooltip: L("Line width of support. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Resolve default/percentage/auto widths and each extrusion role; measure emitted segment width rather than use one global width.

settings.label: Bridge
settings.tooltip:
L("Line width of the Bridge. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
" "Recommended to use with a higher Bridge density or Bridge flow ratio.

" "The maximum value is 100% or the nozzle diameter.
" "If set to 0, the line width will match the Internal solid infill width, or the nozzle diameter for thick bridges.")
settings.handling: Resolve default/percentage/auto widths and each extrusion role; measure emitted segment width rather than use one global width.

settings.label: Seam position
settings.tooltip: L("This is the starting position for each part of the outer wall.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Staggered inner seams
settings.tooltip: L("This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Seam gap
settings.tooltip: L("In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.\n" "This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the nozzle diameter. The default value for this parameter is 10%.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)
settings.tooltip: L("Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Conditional scarf joint
settings.tooltip: L("Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Conditional angle threshold
settings.tooltip: L( "This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam.\nIf the maximum angle within the perimeter loop " "exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Conditional overhang threshold
settings.tooltip: L("This option determines the overhang threshold for the application of scarf joint seams. If the unsupported portion " "of the perimeter is less than this threshold, scarf joint seams will be applied. The default threshold is set at 40% " "of the external wall's width. Due to performance considerations, the degree of overhang is estimated.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Scarf joint speed
settings.tooltip: L( "This option sets the printing speed for scarf joints. It is recommended to print scarf joints at a slow speed (less than 100 " "mm/s). It's also advisable to enable 'Extrusion rate smoothing' if the set speed varies significantly from the speed of the " "outer or inner walls.\n\nIf the speed specified here is higher than the speed of the outer or inner walls, the printer will default " "to the slower of the two speeds. When specified as a percentage (e.g., 80%), the speed is calculated based on the respective " "outer or inner wall speed. The default value is set to 100%.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Scarf start height
settings.tooltip: L("Start height of the scarf.\n" "This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Scarf around entire wall
settings.tooltip: L("The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Scarf length
settings.tooltip: L("Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Scarf steps
settings.tooltip: L("Minimum number of segments of each scarf.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Scarf joint flow ratio
settings.tooltip: L("This factor affects the amount of material for scarf joints.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
settings.tooltip: L("Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Role based wipe speed
settings.tooltip: L("The wipe speed is determined by the speed of the current extrusion role. " "e.g. if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Wipe speed
settings.tooltip: L("The wipe speed is determined by the speed setting specified in this configuration. " "If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 80%), it will be calculated based on the travel speed setting above. " "The default value for this parameter is 80%.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Wipe on loops
settings.tooltip: L("To minimize the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, a small inward movement is executed before the extruder leaves the loop.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Wipe inward
settings.tooltip:
L("Applies only to external walls, including hole boundaries. Moves the hot nozzle toward the " "inner walls during wiping to reduce reheating of freshly printed plastic and seam marks.

" "Especially useful at layer heights below 0.1 mm, where wipe marks are more visible.

" "Uses the regular wipe where the outer wall has no adjacent inner wall, such as in single-wall " "areas, or if no supported inward path can be found, for example at tight corners or seam gaps.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Wipe inward distance
settings.tooltip:
L("The distance the wipe path is shifted away from the external perimeter, specified in millimeters " "or as a percentage of the actual outer-wall extrusion width.

" "For example, 50% shifts the path by half of the outer-wall width. The effective offset is limited " "by both the actual outer-wall width and the available spacing to the adjacent wall, so values " "above 100% or an equivalent absolute distance have no additional effect. " "Set to 0 to disable the offset.

" "With Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall order, the offset is limited to 50% of the actual " "outer-wall width because the adjacent inner wall is printed after the outer wall. " "This also applies to equivalent distances specified in millimeters.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Wipe before external loop
settings.tooltip: L("To minimize visibility of potential overextrusion at the start of an external perimeter when printing with " "Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order, the de-retraction is performed slightly on the inside from the " "start of the external perimeter. That way any potential over extrusion is hidden from the outside surface.\n\n" "This is useful when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order as in these modes it is more likely " "an external perimeter is printed immediately after a de-retraction move.")
settings.handling: Seam ramps, scarf Z/flow/speed and wipe/loop moves change pressure and clearance. Mark seams/wipes and settling zones; do not fit a constant-gap knee through them.

settings.label: Slice gap closing radius
settings.tooltip: L("Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. " "The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Resolution
settings.tooltip: L("The G-code path is generated after simplifying the contour of models to avoid too many points and G-code lines. Smaller values mean higher resolution and more time required to slice.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Arc fitting
settings.tooltip:
L("Fit G2 and G3 arc moves to the toolpaths. Walls and surfaces are fitted within the resolution, while " "sparse infill, supports and the wipe tower use fixed tolerances.
" " - Disabled: only straight G1 moves are used.
" " - Enabled: arcs are fitted to all toolpaths.
" " - Sparse infill only: arcs are fitted to the sparse infill only, which shortens the G-code of " "curved infill patterns without affecting the walls and surfaces.

" "Note: For Klipper machines, Disabled is recommended. Klipper splits arcs back into line segments, " "which lowers the surface quality and can increase the print time.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: X-Y hole compensation
settings.tooltip: L("Holes in objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the set value. Positive values make holes bigger and negative values make holes smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when objects have assembly issues.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: X-Y contour compensation
settings.tooltip: L("Contours of objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the set value. Positive values make contours bigger and negative values make contours smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when objects have assembly issues.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Elephant foot compensation
settings.tooltip: L("This shrinks the first layer on the build plate to compensate for elephant foot effect.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Elephant foot layers density
settings.tooltip: L("Density of internal solid infill for Elephant foot layers compensation.\n" "The initial value for the second layer is set.\n" "Subsequent layers become linearly denser by the height specified in elefant_foot_compensation_layers.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Elephant foot compensation layers
settings.tooltip: L("The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. " "The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then " "the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Precise wall
settings.tooltip: L("Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency.\n\nNote: This option " "will be ignored for outer-inner or inner-outer-inner wall sequences.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Precise Z height
settings.tooltip: L("Enable this to get precise Z height of object after slicing. " "It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. " "Note that this is an experimental parameter.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Convert holes to polyholes
settings.tooltip: L("Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes." " Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole." "\nSee http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Polyhole detection margin
settings.tooltip: L("Maximum defection of a point to the estimated radius of the circle." "\nAs cylinders are often exported as triangles of varying size, points may not be on the circle circumference." " This setting allows you some leeway to broaden the detection." "\nIn mm or in % of the radius.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Polyhole twist
settings.tooltip: L("Rotate the polyhole every layer.")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Maximum Polyhole edge count
settings.tooltip: L("Maximum number of polyhole edges" "\nThis setting limits the amount of edges a polyhole can have")
settings.handling: Geometry compensation, curve resolution and Z rounding alter toolpath position, spacing and contact history. Record actual path/mesh coordinates and resolved dimensions.

settings.label: Ironing type
settings.tooltip: L("Ironing uses a small flow to print at the same height of a surface to make flat surfaces smoother. This setting controls which layers are being ironed.")
settings.handling: Ironing has intentionally different flow/gap/contact. Keep it separate; if present on a one-layer part it is not ordinary first-layer deposition.

settings.label: Ironing Pattern
settings.tooltip: L("The pattern that will be used when ironing.")
settings.handling: Ironing has intentionally different flow/gap/contact. Keep it separate; if present on a one-layer part it is not ordinary first-layer deposition.

settings.label: Ironing flow
settings.tooltip: L("This is the amount of material to be extruded during ironing. It is relative to the flow of normal layer height. Too high a value will result in overextrusion on the surface.")
settings.handling: Ironing has intentionally different flow/gap/contact. Keep it separate; if present on a one-layer part it is not ordinary first-layer deposition.

settings.label: Ironing line spacing
settings.tooltip: L("This is the distance between the lines used for ironing.")
settings.handling: Ironing has intentionally different flow/gap/contact. Keep it separate; if present on a one-layer part it is not ordinary first-layer deposition.

settings.label: Ironing inset
settings.tooltip: L("The distance to keep from the edges. A value of 0 sets this to half of the nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Ironing has intentionally different flow/gap/contact. Keep it separate; if present on a one-layer part it is not ordinary first-layer deposition.

settings.label: Ironing angle offset
settings.tooltip: L("The angle of ironing lines offset from the top surface.")
settings.handling: Ironing has intentionally different flow/gap/contact. Keep it separate; if present on a one-layer part it is not ordinary first-layer deposition.

settings.label: Fixed ironing angle
settings.tooltip: L("Use a fixed absolute angle for ironing.")
settings.handling: Ironing has intentionally different flow/gap/contact. Keep it separate; if present on a one-layer part it is not ordinary first-layer deposition.

settings.label: Z contouring enabled
settings.tooltip: L("Enable Z-layer contouring (aka Z-layer anti-aliasing).")
settings.handling: Nonplanar/Z-contouring moves can change clearance independently of a global offset. Disable ordinary knee learning for nonplanar segments unless explicitly supported.

settings.label: Minimize wall height angle
settings.tooltip: L("Reduce the height of top-surface perimeters to match the model edge height.\n" "Affects perimeters with a slope greater than this angle (degrees).\n" "A reasonable value is 35. Set to 0 to disable.")
settings.handling: Nonplanar/Z-contouring moves can change clearance independently of a global offset. Disable ordinary knee learning for nonplanar segments unless explicitly supported.

settings.label: Minimum Z height
settings.tooltip: L("Minimum Z-layer height.\n" "Also controls the slicing plane.")
settings.handling: Nonplanar/Z-contouring moves can change clearance independently of a global offset. Disable ordinary knee learning for nonplanar segments unless explicitly supported.

settings.label: Don't alternate fill direction
settings.tooltip: L("Disable alternating fill direction when using Z contouring.")
settings.handling: Nonplanar/Z-contouring moves can change clearance independently of a global offset. Disable ordinary knee learning for nonplanar segments unless explicitly supported.

settings.label: Wall generator
settings.tooltip: L("The classic wall generator produces walls with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas, gap-fill is used. The Arachne engine produces walls with variable extrusion width.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Wall transitioning threshold angle
settings.tooltip: L("When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with" " an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be " "printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces " "the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Wall transitioning filter margin
settings.tooltip:
L("Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This " "margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum wall width " "- margin, 2 * Minimum wall width + margin].

Increasing this margin " "reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion " "starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to " "under- or overextrusion problems.

" "It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Wall transition length
settings.tooltip: L("When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall segments. It\'s expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Wall distribution count
settings.tooltip: L("The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be " "spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: First layer minimum wall width
settings.tooltip: L("The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set " "to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Minimum wall width
settings.tooltip: L("Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) " "of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature," " the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. " "It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Minimum feature size
settings.tooltip: L("Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, " "while features thicker than than this value will be widened to the minimum wall width. " "It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Minimum wall length
settings.tooltip: L("Adjust this value to prevent short, unclosed walls from being printed, which could increase print time. " "The value is a multiple of the wall width. Higher values remove more and longer walls.\n\n" "NOTE: Bottom and top surfaces will not be affected by this value to prevent visual gaps on the outside of the model. " "Adjust 'One wall threshold' in the 'Walls and surfaces' settings below to adjust the sensitivity of what is considered a top-surface. " "'One wall threshold' is only visible if this setting is set above the default value of 0.5, or if single-wall top surfaces is enabled.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Maximum wall resolution
settings.tooltip: L("This value determines the smallest wall line segment length in mm. " "The smaller you set this value, the more accurate and precise the walls will be.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Maximum wall deviation
settings.tooltip: L("The maximum deviation allowed when reducing the resolution for the 'Maximum wall resolution' setting. If you increase this, " "the print will be less accurate, but the G-code will be smaller. 'Maximum wall deviation' limits 'Maximum wall resolution', " "so if the two conflict, 'Maximum wall deviation' takes precedence.")
settings.handling: Arachne can vary local bead widths and transitions despite identical nominal settings. Keep generator and local widths; exclude transitions or model separately.

settings.label: Walls printing order
settings.tooltip:
L("Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls.

" "Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighbouring perimeter while printing. " "However, this option results in slightly reduced surface quality as the external perimeter is deformed by being squashed to the internal perimeter.

" "Use Inner/Outer/Inner for the best external surface finish and dimensional accuracy as the external wall is printed undisturbed from an internal perimeter. " "However, overhang performance will reduce as there is no internal perimeter to print the external wall against. " "This option requires a minimum of 3 walls to be effective as it prints the internal walls from the 3rd perimeter onwards first, " "then the external perimeter and, finally, the first internal perimeter. " "This option is recommended over the Outer/Inner option in most cases.

" "Use Outer/Inner for the same external wall quality and dimensional accuracy benefits of Inner/Outer/Inner option. " "However, the Z seams will appear less consistent as the first extrusion of a new layer starts on a visible surface.")
settings.handling: Capture effective role flow ratios, first-layer switches and wall/infill ordering. Area compensation and overlaps change deposition and subsequent contact; fingerprint plus per-role/segment context.

settings.label: Print infill first
settings.tooltip: L("Order of wall/infill. When the tickbox is unchecked the walls are printed first, which works best in most cases.\n\nPrinting infill first may help with extreme overhangs as the walls have the neighbouring infill to adhere to. However, the infill will slightly push out the printed walls where it is attached to them, resulting in a worse external surface finish. It can also cause the infill to shine through the external surfaces of the part.")
settings.handling: Capture effective role flow ratios, first-layer switches and wall/infill ordering. Area compensation and overlaps change deposition and subsequent contact; fingerprint plus per-role/segment context.

settings.label: Wall loop direction
settings.tooltip:
L("The direction which the contour wall loops are extruded when looking down from the top.
Holes are printed in the opposite direction to the contour to maintain alignment with layers whose contour polygons are incomplete and change direction, also partially forming the contour of a hole.

This option will be disabled if spiral vase mode is enabled.")
settings.handling: Capture effective role flow ratios, first-layer switches and wall/infill ordering. Area compensation and overlaps change deposition and subsequent contact; fingerprint plus per-role/segment context.

settings.label: Flow ratio
settings.tooltip: L("The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. " "This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. " "The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. " "You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow." "\n\nThe final object flow ratio is this value multiplied by the filament flow ratio.")
settings.handling: Capture effective role flow ratios, first-layer switches and wall/infill ordering. Area compensation and overlaps change deposition and subsequent contact; fingerprint plus per-role/segment context.

settings.label: Top surface flow ratio
settings.tooltip: L("This factor affects the amount of material for top solid infill. " "You can decrease it slightly to have smooth surface finish.\n\n" "The actual top surface flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.")
settings.handling: Capture effective role flow ratios, first-layer switches and wall/infill ordering. Area compensation and overlaps change deposition and subsequent contact; fingerprint plus per-role/segment context.

settings.label: Bottom surface flow ratio
settings.tooltip: L("This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill.\n\n" "The actual bottom solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.")
settings.handling: Capture effective role flow ratios, first-layer switches and wall/infill ordering. Area compensation and overlaps change deposition and subsequent contact; fingerprint plus per-role/segment context.

settings.label: Set other flow ratios
settings.tooltip: L("Change flow ratios for other extrusion path types.")
settings.handling: Capture effective role flow ratios, first-layer switches and wall/infill ordering. Area compensation and overlaps change deposition and subsequent contact; fingerprint plus per-role/segment context.

settings.label: First layer flow ratio
settings.tooltip: L("This factor affects the amount of material on the first layer for the extrusion path roles listed in this section.\n\n" "For the first layer, the actual flow ratio for each path role (does not affect brims and skirts) will be multiplied by this value.")
settings.handling: Capture effective role flow ratios, first-layer switches and wall/infill ordering. Area compensation and overlaps change deposition and subsequent contact; fingerprint plus per-role/segment context.

settings.label: Outer wall flow ratio
settings.tooltip: L("This factor affects the amount of material for outer walls.\n\n" "The actual outer wall flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.")
settings.handling: Capture effective role flow ratios, first-layer switches and wall/infill ordering. Area compensation and overlaps change deposition and subsequent contact; fingerprint plus per-role/segment context.

settings.label: External bridge density

L("Controls the density (spacing) of external bridge lines.

" " - Pros: Can create a string-like first layer. Faster and with better cooling because there is more space for air to circulate around the extruded bridge.

settings.label: Extra bridge layers (beta)
settings.tooltip:
L("This option enables the generation of an extra bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges.

" "Extra bridge layers help improve bridge appearance and reliability, as the solid infill is better supported. " "This is especially useful in fast printers, where the bridge and solid infill speeds vary greatly. " "The extra bridge layer results in reduced pillowing on top surfaces, as well as reduced separation of the external bridge layer from its surrounding perimeters.

" "It is generally recommended to set this to at least 'External bridge only', unless specific issues with the sliced model are found.

" "Options:
" "1. Disabled - does not generate second bridge layers. This is the default and is set for compatibility purposes
" "2. External bridge only - generates second bridge layers for external-facing bridges only. Please note that small bridges that are shorter " "or narrower than the set number of perimeters will be skipped as they would not benefit from a second bridge layer. If generated, " "the second bridge layer will be extruded parallel to the first bridge layer to reinforce the bridge strength
" "3. Internal bridge only - generates second bridge layers for internal bridges over sparse infill only. " "Please note that the internal bridges count towards the top shell layer count of your model. " "The second internal bridge layer will be extruded as close to perpendicular to the first as possible. " "If multiple regions in the same island, with varying bridge angles are present, the last region of that island will be selected as the angle reference
" "4. Apply to all - generates second bridge layers for both internal and external-facing bridges
")
settings.handling: Bridge flow, density, thickness and unsupported cross-section use different geometry. Exclude bridge roles from ordinary bed-contact fitting; retain settings for provenance.

settings.label: Filter out small internal bridges
settings.tooltip:
L("This option can help reduce pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.
" "By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed " "directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding up printing without " "too much compromise on top surface quality.
" "However, in heavily slanted or curved models, especially where too low a sparse infill density " "is used, this may result in curling of the unsupported solid infill, causing pillowing.
" "Enabling limited filtering or no filtering will print internal bridge layer over slightly " "unsupported internal solid infill. The options below control the sensitivity of the filtering, " "i.e. they control where internal bridges are created:
" "1. Filter - enables this option. This is the default behavior and works well in most cases
" "2. Limited filtering - creates internal bridges on heavily slanted surfaces while avoiding " "unnecessary bridges. This works well for most difficult models
" "3. No filtering - creates internal bridges on every potential internal overhang. This option is " "useful for heavily slanted top surface models

settings.label: Adaptive density (experimental)
settings.tooltip:
L("Grades the Gyroid and TPMS infill inside the object: its cells grow from the surface of the " "object towards its center. The sparse infill density is used at the surface and the interior " "density at the center.
" "Distance warp, Smooth blend and Stepped shells follow the distance to the nearest surface, " "including the top and bottom, with the interior density at the point farthest from it:
" " - Distance warp: one continuous pattern, stretched and sheared where the distance changes " "across directions, as in plates and long parts.
" " - Smooth blend: the patterns of neighbouring densities blended into each other, with small " "loops where they meet.
" " - Stepped shells: shells of the regular pattern at densities about 1.5 times apart, their " "lines joined along the shell boundaries.
" " - Lobes: follows the 3D shape of the object, including its top and bottom. Every lobe, a part " "joined to the rest by a narrower neck, is graded towards its own center.
" " - Normal Z, Y or X: follows the sections of the object normal to that axis, so the density " "does not change along it.")

L("Enable this option to slow down printing in areas where perimeters may have curled upwards.
" "For example, additional slowdown will be applied when printing overhangs on sharp corners like the " "front of the Benchy hull, reducing curling which compounds over multiple layers.

" "It is generally recommended to have this option switched on unless your printer cooling is powerful enough or the " "print speed is slow enough that perimeter curling does not happen.
" "If printing with a high external perimeter speed, this parameter may introduce wall artifacts when slowing down, " "due to the potentially large variance in print speeds causing the extruder to be unable to keep up with the requested flow change.
" "Root cause of these artifacts is most likely PA tuning being slightly off, especially when combined " "with a high PA smooth time.

" "Recommendations when enabling this option:
" "1. Reduce Pressure Advance smooth time to 0.015 - 0.02 so the extruder reacts quickly to the speed changes.
" "2. Increase the minimum print speeds to limit the magnitude of the slowdown and reduce the variance between fast and slow segments.
" "3. If artifacts still appear, enable Extrusion Rate Smoothing (ERS) to further smooth the flow transitions.

" "Note: When this option is enabled, overhang perimeters are treated like overhangs, meaning the overhang speed is " "applied even if the overhanging perimeter is part of a bridge.

settings.label: Leading brim length
settings.tooltip:
L("Belt printers only. Extends the brim AHEAD of the object along the belt, on " "every downhill-facing edge of its contact area - both the object's first " "contact with the belt and any island that lands later. This apron is laid " "onto the belt before the object reaches it, so the leading edge has " "something already stuck down to hold on to.

" "Measured on the belt surface, and added on top of Brim width: the brim " "reaches Brim-object gap + Leading brim length + Brim width ahead of the " "object. Set Brim-object gap to 0, or the apron will not touch the object it " "is meant to anchor.

" "On a tilted belt each layer lays one strip of the brim, so the thickness of " "the resulting brim sheet is set by flow rather than by layer height. Use " "Brim flow ratio to tune it.

" "Set to 0 to disable.")
settings.handling: Brim flow, gap and geometry change bed-contact extrusion near parts. Brim is not the model role and its first-layer flow multiplier treatment differs; retain masks/pressure history.

" "Measured on the belt surface, and added on top of Brim width: the brim " "reaches Brim-object gap + Brim width + Extra brim width to either side of " "the object. To extend the brim ahead of the object instead, use Leading brim " "length.

" "Set to 0 to disable.")

settings.label: Intra-layer order
settings.tooltip:
L("Order in which object instances are visited within a single layer, which controls how much " "travel is spent moving between them.

" "Default: nearest-neighbor chaining, refined with 2-opt and crossing removal. A good general " "choice.
" "As object list: instances are printed in the same order as the object list, without any path " "optimization. Use it when you need a predictable, manually controlled order.
" "Best of all (shortest path): every strategy is evaluated and the shortest one is used. The " "object instance order is decided once for the whole print, while the ordering of individual " "islands is decided per layer, so different layers may end up using different strategies. " "Slightly slower to slice.
" "Snake: serpentine row-by-row traversal, refined with 2-opt. Well suited to regular grids of " "many small parts.

" "With multiple filaments or tools in the same layer, minimizing tool changes takes priority: " "objects are grouped by filament first and this setting only orders the instances within each " "filament group, so the overall sequence may not look like the shortest path across the plate.")
settings.handling: Vase, object sequence, mixed layer identity and timelapse/wrapping moves can invalidate first-layer markers and constant clearance. Exclude incompatible modes until explicit support.

settings.label: Fuzzy skin generator mode
settings.tooltip:
L("Fuzzy skin generation mode. Works only with Arachne!
" "Displacement: Сlassic mode when the pattern is formed by shifting the nozzle sideways from the original path.
" "Extrusion: The mode when the pattern formed by the amount of extruded plastic. " "This is the fast and straight algorithm without unnecessary nozzle shake that gives a smooth pattern. " "But it is more useful for forming loose walls in the entire they array.
" "Combined: Joint mode [Displacement] + [Extrusion]. The appearance of the walls is similar to [Displacement] Mode, but it leaves no pores between the perimeters.

" "Attention! The [Extrusion] and [Combined] modes works only the fuzzy_skin_thickness parameter not more than the thickness of printed loop. " "At the same time, the width of the extrusion for a particular layer should also not be below a certain level. " "It is usually equal 15-25% of a layer height. Therefore, the maximum fuzzy skin thickness with a perimeter width of 0.4 mm and a layer height of 0.2 mm will be 0.4-(0.2*0.25)=±0.35mm! " "If you enter a higher parameter than this, the error Flow::spacing() will displayed, and the model will not be sliced. You can choose this number until this error is repeated." )
settings.handling: Fuzzy skin can apply to layer1; point spacing/noise/width perturbations affect flow and inertia. Exclude affected paths from a flat steady-state knee fit.

settings.label: Fuzzy skin noise type
settings.tooltip:
L("Noise type to use for fuzzy skin generation:
" "Classic: Classic uniform random noise.
" "Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture.
" "Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier.
" "Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. Creates marble-like textures.
" "Voronoi: Divides the surface into voronoi cells, and displaces each one by a random amount. Creates a patchwork texture.
" "Ripple: Uniform ripple pattern that ripples left and right of the original path. Repeating pattern, woven appearance.")
settings.handling: Fuzzy skin can apply to layer1; point spacing/noise/width perturbations affect flow and inertia. Exclude affected paths from a flat steady-state knee fit.

settings.label: High precision G-code (experimental)
settings.tooltip: L("Write X, Y, Z, I and J with 4 decimal places instead of 3, and E with 6 instead of 5, to reduce " "rounding errors in the G-code. With relative E distances, the rounding error of each move is also " "carried over to the next one. Supports are removed after printing, so they keep the standard " "precision. This may help stabilize extrusion with small nozzles (e.g. 0.2 mm) and " "thin layers (e.g. 0.08 mm or less), where each move extrudes so little material that rounding errors " "matter most. The effect depends strongly on how well the rest of the settings are tuned and may be hard " "to notice unless the print profile is well calibrated.\n\nThe G-code file becomes about 10 percent larger, " "which may slow down printers that parse G-code slowly.")
settings.handling: Coordinate/E quantization changes can matter on thin layers; record precision and emitted values.

additional_material_machine_dependencies.label: Enable adaptive pressure advance (beta)
additional_material_machine_dependencies.tooltip:
L("With increasing print speeds (and hence increasing volumetric flow through the nozzle) and increasing accelerations, " "it has been observed that the effective PA value typically decreases. " "This means that a single PA value is not always 100% optimal for all features and a compromise value is usually used " "that does not cause too much bulging on features with lower flow speed and accelerations while also not causing gaps on faster features.

" "This feature aims to address this limitation by modeling the response of your printer's extrusion system depending " "on the volumetric flow speed and acceleration it is printing at. Internally, it generates a fitted model that can extrapolate the needed pressure " "advance for any given volumetric flow speed and acceleration, which is then emitted to the printer depending on the current print conditions.

" "When enabled, the pressure advance value above is overridden. However, a reasonable default value above is " "strongly recommended to act as a fallback and for when tool changing.

")

additional_material_machine_dependencies.label: Adaptive pressure advance measurements (beta)
additional_material_machine_dependencies.tooltip:
L("Add sets of pressure advance (PA) values, the volumetric flow speeds and accelerations they were measured at, separated by a comma. " "One set of values per line. For example
" "0.04,3.96,3000
0.033,3.96,10000
0.029,7.91,3000
0.026,7.91,10000

" "How to calibrate:
" "1. Run the pressure advance test for at least 3 speeds per acceleration value. It is recommended that the test is run " "for at least the speed of the external perimeters, the speed of the internal perimeters and the fastest feature " "print speed in your profile (usually its the sparse or solid infill). Then run them for the same speeds for the slowest and fastest print accelerations, " "and no faster than the recommended maximum acceleration as given by the Klipper input shaper
" "2. Take note of the optimal PA value for each volumetric flow speed and acceleration. You can find the flow number by selecting " "flow from the color scheme drop down and move the horizontal slider over the PA pattern lines. The number should be visible " "at the bottom of the page. The ideal PA value should be decreasing the higher the volumetric flow is. " "If it is not, confirm that your extruder is functioning correctly. The slower and with less acceleration you print, " "the larger the range of acceptable PA values. If no difference is visible, use the PA value from the faster test
" "3. Enter the triplets of PA values, Flow and Accelerations in the text box here and save your filament profile.")

additional_material_machine_dependencies.label: Chamber temperature
additional_material_machine_dependencies.tooltip:
L("For high-temperature materials like ABS, ASA, PC, and PA, a higher chamber temperature can help " "suppress or reduce warping and potentially lead to higher interlayer bonding strength. " "However, at the same time, a higher chamber temperature will reduce the efficiency of air " "filtration for ABS and ASA.

" "For PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA, and other low-temperature materials, this option should be disabled " "(set to 0) as the chamber temperature should be low to avoid extruder clogging caused by " "material softening at the heat break.

" "If enabled, this parameter also sets a G-code variable named chamber_temperature, which can be " "used to pass the desired chamber temperature to your print start macro, or a heat soak macro " "like this:
PRINT_START (other variables) CHAMBER_TEMP=[chamber_temperature]
" "This may be useful if your printer does not support M141/M191 commands, or if you desire " "to handle heat soaking in the print start macro if no active chamber heater is installed." )
